analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/inference.md gains a paragraph at head lines 790-806 describing PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, a per-prefix-cache-scope reuse of token IDs for rendered chat-template pieces. It also describes ChatTemplateLoopRewrites (linear-time Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS template rendering), a load-time comparison, sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on a mismatch, and the kill switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0. No code or control changes are in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete regression. I examined the surrounding base text (lines 416-1235) and only the new paragraph is a change.

Security-relevant claims the paragraph makes, which relate to T-041 (cross-tenant cache sharing and TTFT timing oracle, SEC-035) and A-001:
- Reuse "never crosses a cache scope". This is consistent with the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping in T-041. The paragraph describes a new in-memory cache of prompt-derived token IDs. T-041 does not currently list it, so the threat model may need to add a note on its scope key, lifetime, memory residency and eviction.
- Reuse is scoped by the authenticated cache scope and is not shared across accounts. Per the doc, standalone/no-scope behavior is unspecified here.
- A same-scope TTFT oracle is possible and is already an accepted risk.
- Parallel encoding on up to four cores is a minor resource consideration.

I cannot verify the implementation in PromptTokenCache.swift (scope keying, no cross-scope leakage, bounded size, zeroization, whether the cache is on without a scope). A follow-up pass on that source should check these. I flag this as an unverified contract, not a finding.
